property_summary: The owner state variable should only be changeable by the current owner (via an onlyOwner-protected function), but the mutant allows any caller to change it because the onlyOwner modifier was removed.
For any caller who is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership must not change the owner; the reference enforces this via onlyOwner, but the buggy version allows any caller to change it.
After transferOwnership is called by the current owner with any address, the owner state variable must be updated to the new owner; the mutant leaves owner unchanged.
Only the current owner can successfully call owned(), but after the bug's removal of the check, any caller can do so.
The owner can always successfully call owned(); the bug makes the modifier always revert, so the call fails.

For any caller, calling c.owned() reverts if and only if the caller is not the owner in the reference contract; the bug makes it always revert regardless of the caller, so an owner's call to owned() fails.
A call to owned() never reverts when called by a non-owner before and after ownership is transferred to them; the bug makes it always revert.
For any non-zero address newOwner, after the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the newOwner's subsequent call to owned() succeeds; the bug always reverts.
For any address, calling c.owned() reverts if and only if the caller is not the current owner; the bug makes it always revert, so an owner's call to owned() fails, breaking the rule.

The owned() function in the reference contract reverts for any non-owner, while the buggy version succeeds for all callers; thus for any caller, reference success implies caller is owner, but the buggy version allows non-owners to succeed.
